title: Dhokra
overview: Dhokra is a lost-wax metal casting craft. Follow the nine steps from raw clay to a polished brass artifact.

steps.title: Clay preparation
steps.description: Clay is prepared using soil, rice husk and water to create the internal core.

steps.title: Shaping the clay core
steps.description: The crude clay core is shaped by hand into the rough form of the piece. It has no metallic appearance yet.

steps.title: Dhuna and beeswax
steps.description: Dhuna and beeswax are prepared as the raw material for the wax work. This step covers material preparation only.

steps.title: Black wax strips
steps.description: A wax machine presses the prepared wax into thin black strips.

steps.title: Wax replica
steps.description: Black wax strips are wrapped over the clay core to build the detailed wax replica. No brass appears at this stage.

steps.title: Clay mould
steps.description: Three layers of clay are applied over the wax replica, from thin to medium to thick, to build the mould.

steps.title: Lost wax
steps.description: The mould is heated so the wax melts and runs out, leaving an internal cavity in the shape of the piece.

steps.title: Metal casting
steps.description: Molten metal is poured into the mould, fills the cavity, then cools and sets.

steps.title: Final artifact
steps.description: The mould is broken, and the casting is cleaned and polished to reveal the finished artifact.
